steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: NEA = Non-Exam Assessment, worth 50% of GCSE D&T. Students complete a single design-and-make task from a choice of contextual challenges set by AQA. Approximately 35 hours of supervised time.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: NEA structure: Section 1 - Investigating (research, design brief, specification), Section 2 - Designing (ideas, development, modelling), Section 3 - Making (manufacturing the prototype), Section 4 - Analysing and Evaluating (testing against specification, improvements).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Portfolio: A3 format (or digital equivalent), 20-30 pages recommended. Each section must be clearly labelled. Include photographs of making, annotated sketches, test results, evaluation against specification points.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marking criteria: AO1 - Investigating (10%), AO2 - Designing (20%), AO3 - Making (30%), AO4 - Analysing and Evaluating (15%). Each AO has specific mark bands - read the criteria and target the top band.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the four sections of the D&T NEA and what each must include. | Explain why it is important to evaluate the final prototype against the original specification. | A student has spent 15 hours on research and has only 5 hours left for making and evaluation. What advice would you give?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Each NEA section must be clearly labelled with headings - moderators need to find evidence quickly Photograph EVERY stage of making - you cannot go back and retake photos later Evaluate against EVERY specification point - missed points mean missed marks
